children: Gujarat-based Tirupati Forge has received an industrial licence under the Arms Act, 1959, to manufacture empty artillery shells, marking the company's entry into the defence manufacturing sector.

The NSE-listed precision engineering and forging company plans to begin pilot production in December 2026, subject to trials and required approvals. The initial production capacity is expected to be 150,000 shells annually.

The licence covers artillery shells in 105mm, 120mm, 122mm, 125mm, 130mm, 152mm and 155mm calibres. For the 155mm category, the licence includes HE M107, HE L15A1, Extended Range Full Bore (ERFB), ERFB Base Bleed (BB) and ERFB Boat Tail (BT) variants.

“This licence allows us to enter a new area of defence manufacturing. We will focus on building production capacity and meeting the quality and safety requirements of the defence sector,” said Hitesh Thummar, Chairman and Managing Director of Tirupati Forge.
The company said it will initially focus on manufacturing empty artillery shells and leverage its existing engineering and manufacturing capabilities to develop the new business.

The move comes as India seeks to expand domestic defence production and increase the participation of private-sector manufacturers in the defence supply chain. According to government data cited by the company, India's defence production reached Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY2025-26, while defence exports stood at Rs 38,424 crore.

Tirupati Forge is also exploring technology, manufacturing and supply-chain partnerships with Indian and international companies. The company said such partnerships could support capacity expansion and help it explore overseas markets, subject to regulatory approvals.
“Our aim is to build this into a long-term manufacturing business. We will look at domestic requirements as well as international opportunities as we increase our capabilities,” Thummar said.
The company plans to scale its defence manufacturing operations following the completion of trials and other regulatory requirements, with the initial focus remaining on empty artillery shells.
